newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber slow, Thai news to hit longs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber slow, Thai news to hit longs.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market struggled on Tuesday due to weak demand, dealers said.
They said news Thailand will refrain from buying RSS3 grade rubber will hit those holding long positions in the market.
"The longs will run," a dealer said when asked about his reaction to the news by Thai Deputy Agriculture Minister Grich Gongpechara that Bangkok will not buy rubber in the meantime.
But another dealer said any impact will be limited.
"One person or a government cannot help this market. What we need are orders and prices won't really improve unless we see some orders," the trader said.
Trading remained thin with Bridgestone the only major consumer said to be still mulling offers for SIR20 rubber.
"Bridgestone is still looking but everybody else is sidelined," a dealer said.
"Sellers are also reluctant to sell because they find prices too low at the moment," a trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen unchanged at 116.75 U.S. cents a kg. May RSS1 was seen at 166.00-168.00 Singapore cents (US$1.15-$1.16) a kg from 167.75 cents.
May TSR20 was seen at 156.75 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 157.50 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
